intro.text: One of Shallan Davar's older brothers, a lighteyed Veden and the youngest son of House Davar.
One of Shallan Davar's older brothers, a lighteyed Veden whose gambling has long troubled their house.
One of Shallan Davar's older brothers, who now lives in Urithiru with the rest of his family.

items.text: Born Van Jushu, the youngest of the Davar brothers, Jushu felt that his father favoured Helaran and Shallan, and he suffered many of Lin's rages. He comforted Shallan on the night their mother died.

As a teenager Jushu turned to gambling and heavy drinking, even stealing from his father to fund them. Sent to check on the outer Davar lands, he ran up debts with a bookmaker named Mill, whose thugs beat him and brought him to the estate. Lin refused to pay, so Shallan offered her brothers' daggers and her own necklace to settle the debt.

When the family's fortunes suddenly improved, Jushu alone questioned where the new ore deposits came from. On the night Lin and Balat came to blows, Jushu and Wikim watched in horror, and when Lin collapsed, Jushu found the broken Davar Soulcaster in his pocket.

With their father dead, the siblings faced crushing debts. While Shallan left Jah Keved to find a solution, Jushu helped Balat quietly sell off their possessions to keep the family afloat, drawing on his long experience of selling things he had stolen.

After the Battle of Thaylen Field, Jushu and his brothers arrived in Urithiru, worn and thin, and attended Shallan's wedding to Adolin. There he still had to be watched so he wouldn't pawn things for gambling money.

appearance.text: A lighteyed man, probably with the Davar family's red hair, who grows plump in times of excess. He has scars on both wrists.

personality.text: A happy, smiling child, Jushu is still quicker to laugh than his twin, and turns to gallows humour even in his darkest moments.

Jushu struggles with addiction: he gambles anything he has, drinks heavily, and will lie and steal to fund it. Shallan thinks him a good man who can't be blamed for vices born of their father's temper.
